svg.text: M3.13 · What does a table whose primary key has several columns give?
PR #124 · spec §3.4, §3.5, §4.1 · today the database importer (M3.1) refuses such a table · Chinook needs an answer before M3.3
The source: Chinook's PlaylistTrack table
It only links a playlist to a track. Its key is two columns, and each column is also a foreign key.
PlaylistTrack
PlaylistId PK, FK → Playlist │ 1
TrackId PK, FK → Track │ 3402
Example row: PlaylistId=1, TrackId=3402; the settings name PlaylistTrack, Playlist and Track.
Reading 1 · One node per row
PlaylistTrack:1/3402
Playlist:1
Track:3402
PlaylistId
TrackId
• A node per row; its key is the key columns'
values in key order, joined by “/”.
• One edge per foreign key, evidence
…;row=1/3402;field=PlaylistId
A reader asking for Playlist:1's neighbours
sees PlaylistTrack nodes; tracks are 2 hops away.
⚠ The mosaic can never link a playlist
straight to its tracks: a pattern cannot compute
an edge through a node (§5.3: map copies piece
edges; mentions makes edges from mentions).
Reading 2 · One edge per row
CHOSEN: READING 2
Playlist:1
Track:3402
<type from
settings>
• No PlaylistTrack node. One edge per row, from
the row the 1st key column names to the 2nd.
• The table's entry in the settings names the
edge type; other columns become edge props.
• Evidence, no field (the whole row is the fact):
…;table=PlaylistTrack;row=1/3402
• A several-column key that is not exactly two
foreign keys is still refused.
A reader asking for Playlist:1's neighbours
sees its tracks directly.
Why expected: the table exists only to link;
reading 1 can't link directly, reading 3 loses it.
Reading 3 · Still refused
$ mosaic import sqlite …
error: PlaylistTrack has a
primary key of 2 columns (exit 1)
• Same as today: the import names the table
and exits 1; settings must leave it out.
The Chinook tessera and mosaic hold no
playlist-to-track links at all.
Also visible in readings 1 and 2: the key form “1/3402”
in the node id (reading 1) and in the locator's row= value (both). Proposed with it: a key value containing “/” is refused,
as M3.1 already refuses “;”, otherwise ('1/', '2') and ('1', '/2') would give the same key.
Answer on #124: 1, 2 or 3
